resources.string: Reads the on-screen text of Google Pay, PhonePe and Paytm only, to detect the amount, status and payee of a UPI payment for testing. It does not read any other app, does not perform any action on screen, skips password fields, and keeps everything on this phone.
Notification access: off. Used only to cross-check payments; notifications never create records.

Toggle greyed out? Android blocks Accessibility for sideloaded apps until you allow it: Settings → Apps → UPI Detector → ⋮ (top right) → Allow restricted settings. The same \"Allow restricted settings\" step applies on Android 13+ for Notification access. Then come back here.
Removes this record as a duplicate of the earlier one. It cannot be undone.
Pending, failed, credit and flagged payments are not counted in the total.
Everything is kept in memory only: it is lost if the app is force-stopped, the phone restarts or the service is turned off.
No raw screens captured yet. Open GPay, PhonePe or Paytm with the service and raw capture enabled. The last 30 screens are kept in memory only.
No payments detected yet.\nEnable the service, then make a small UPI payment (₹1) in GPay, PhonePe or Paytm. Detections are kept in memory only.
Nothing logged yet. Open GPay, PhonePe or Paytm with the service enabled. The log is kept in memory only.
Clears every detected transaction, log line and raw capture held in memory. Nothing is stored on disk.
Service: OFF. Enable "UPI Detector" in Accessibility settings.
Expense total: ₹%1$s (success, debit, not flagged) Success %2$d · Failed %3$d · Pending %4$d · Flagged %5$d
